source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 702 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 702 was established by Ordinance No. 25852 passed by the Dallas City Council on January 12, 2005. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 702 is established on property generally located on the east line of Abrams Road, south of Forest Lane and LBJ Freeway, and north and south of Timberleaf Drive. The size of PD 702 is approximately 27.6 acres. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Creation Of Areas
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.103. CREATION OF AREAS.

PD 702 is divided into four areas (Areas A, B, C, and D) as shown on the conceptual plan (Exhibit 702A). (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.104. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) Area A is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. Areas B through D are considered to be residential zoning districts. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan. In the event of a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) Except for CR Community Retail District uses in Area A, development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 702B). In the event of a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For all CR Community Retail District uses in Area A, no development plan is required and the provisions of Section 51A-4.702 regarding submission of, or amendments to, a development plan, site analysis plan, conceptual plan, development schedule, and landscape plan do not apply. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Area A. The only main uses permitted in Area A are:

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, those uses permitted in the CR Community Retail District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the CR Community Retail District, as set out in Chapter 51A and subject to installation and maintenance of a six-foot-high screening wall between the CR Community Retail uses and any adjacent multifamily or private street or alley uses. For example, a use permitted in the CR Community Retail District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this area only by SUP, and a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the CR Community Retail District is subject to DIR in this area.

(2) Multifamily uses (permitted by right).

(3) Private streets or alleys, permitted by right, only in the location shown on the conceptual plan as “Proposed Private Drive/Street.” A private street or a private drive in the area of the Proposed Private Drive/Street is subject to the following conditions:

(A) The private street or private drive may serve a cumulative maximum of 516 dwelling units in Areas A and B.

(B) Section 51A-8.503(b) requiring that lots front on a public or private street is waived if the Proposed Private Drive/Street is platted as an access easement that provides adequate access to all lots in Areas A and B.

(C) A maintenance agreement meeting the requirements in Chapter 51A for a private street must be provided prior to replatting of the public street whether the Proposed Private Drive/Street is platted as a private drive or a private street.

(D) Any utilities located in the existing public street in the area of the Proposed Private Drive/Street must be provided with easements satisfactory to the provider prior to replatting of the public street.

(E) If the area of the Proposed Private Drive/Street is abandoned, the utility easements, access easement (if applicable), and maintenance agreement must be recorded immediately upon the effectiveness of the abandonment, and the Property must be replatted to reflect the abandonment.

(b) Area B. The only main uses permitted in Area B are:

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, those uses permitted in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District only by SUP is permitted in this area only by SUP; a use subject to DIR in the MF-2(A) Multifamily District is subject to DIR in this area; etc.

(2) Private streets or alleys, permitted by right, only in the location shown on the conceptual plan as “Proposed Private Drive/Street.” A private street or a private drive in the area of the Proposed Private Drive/Street is subject to all of the conditions in Subsection (a)(3) of this section.

(c) Area C. The only main use permitted in Area C is a private recreation center, club, or area, limited to open space and pedestrian facilities, including, but not limited to, benches, trails, tables, unenclosed gazebos and playground equipment. No enclosed structures are permitted in Area C.

(d) Area D. The only main uses permitted in Area D are:

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, those uses permitted in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District only by SUP is permitted in this area only by SUP; a use subject to DIR in the TH-3(A) Townhouse District is subject to DIR in this area; etc.

(2) Private recreation center, club, or area, limited to one private swimming pool located in City Block S/8151on unit 1-A, as shown on the development plan. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A- 4.217. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. In the event of a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the CR Community Retail District apply in Area A; the yard, lot, and space regulations for the MF-2(A) Multifamily District apply in Area B and Area C; and the yard, lot, and space regulations for the TH-3(A) Townhouse District apply in Area D.

(b) Front yard.

(1) In Areas A and B, for a multifamily use, minimum front yard is as shown on the development plan.

(2) In Area D, for an attached single family use, minimum front yard is as shown on the development plan.

(c) Side and rear yard.

(1) In Areas A and B, for a multifamily use, minimum side and rear yard is as shown on the development plan, but a minimum of five feet is required between exterior walls of multifamily structures.

(2) In Area D, for an attached single family use, minimum side and rear yard is as shown on the development plan, and the single family structure spacing requirement and the side yard requirements of the more restrictive district do not apply.

(d) Density.

(1) In Areas A and B, the cumulative maximum number of dwelling units is 516

(2) For Area D, maximum number of dwelling units is 84. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking/loading requirements for each use.

(b) For existing single family structures in Area D, enclosed parking garages with operable automatic garage doors may be located within the required 20-foot right-of-way line that is adjacent to a street or alley in the locations shown on the development plan.

(c) For attached single family and multifamily uses, off-street parking in Areas A, B, and D must be provided in the locations shown on the development plan.

(d) A public alley, access easement, private driveway, or private street may be used for two- way access to and from off-street parking, and for maneuvering space, without the approval of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Screening And Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.112. SCREENING AND LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Multifamily uses in Area B. For multifamily uses in Area B, the requirements in Section 51A-10.125(b)(1), (the Perimeter Landscape Buffer Strip) do not apply.

(c) Encroachments into the right-of-way. Existing fences, walls, columns or other architectural features as shown on the development plan may project into, or be in, the right-of-way.

(d) Private license granted for existing encroachments.

(1) The city council hereby grants a revocable, non-exclusive license to the owners, or with the written consent of the owner, to the tenants (“property owner”) of all property in this district for the exclusive purpose of authorizing any existing fences, walls, columns or other architectural features (“encroachments”) as shown on the development plan that may project into, or be in, the right-of-way along Forest Springs Drive. A property owner is not required to pay an initial or annual fee for this license. This private license shall not terminate at the end of any specific time period, however, the city council reserves and has the absolute right to terminate this license at will, by resolution passed by the city council, any time such termination becomes necessary. The determination by the city of the necessity for such termination shall be final and binding and the city shall become entitled to possession of the premises without giving any notice and without the necessity of legal proceedings to obtain possession whenever in its judgment the purpose or use of this license is inconsistent with the public use of the right-

of-way or when the purpose or use of this license is likely to become a nuisance or a public safety issue. Upon termination of the license by the director, each property owner shall remove all improvements and installations in the public rights-of-way in a manner satisfactory to the director of public works and transportation.

(2) The property owner shall procure, pay for and keep in full force and effect commercial general liability insurance coverage with an insurance company authorized to do business in the State of Texas and otherwise acceptable to the city, covering, but not limited to, the liability assumed under the license granted herein, with combined single limits of liability for bodily injury and property damage of not less that $1,000,000 for each occurrence, $2,000,000 annual aggregate. Coverage under this liability policy shall be on an “occurrence” basis and the city shall be named as additional insured. Proof of such insurance shall be sent to: Office of Risk Management, City of Dallas, 1500 Marilla, 1/C/North, Dallas, Texas 75201 and the policy shall provide for 30 days prior written notice to the office of risk management of cancellation, expiration, non-renewal or material change in coverage. All subrogation rights for loss or damage against the city are hereby waived to the extent it is covered by this liability insurance policy.

(3) Each property owner shall be responsible for maintaining the encroachments in good repair and condition and to keep the premises safe and from deteriorating in value or condition, at no expense to the city, and the city shall be absolutely exempt from any requirements to make repairs or to maintain the encroachments. The granting of a license for encroachments under this section does not release the property owner from liability in the installation or maintenance of trees, landscaping, and related amenities in the public right-of-way.

(e) Screening in Area A. In Area A, prior to issuance of a certificate of occupancy for any use permitted in the CR Community Retail District (other than private streets or alleys, which are permitted by right in Area A), a six-foot-high screening wall must be installed and maintained between the CR Community Retail use and any adjacent multifamily or private street or alley uses.

(f) Maintenance. All plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.113. SIGNS.

(a) For multifamily uses in Area A, signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. For all other uses in Area A, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) Signs located in Areas B, C, and D must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Guard House
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.114. GUARD HOUSE.

One guard house is permitted in the location shown on the development plan. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Fences
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.115. FENCES.

For multifamily or attached-single family uses, a maximum eight-foot-high fence is permitted in the front yard in the locations shown on the development plan. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) The entire Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(b) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(c) The owner must notify, by certified mail, return receipt requested, the President of the Lake Highlands Area Improvement Association of any subsequent zoning changes, or amendments to the conceptual plan, or development plan on the Property. The notice must be sent at the same time the application is filed with the city to the address on file with the city for the Lake Highlands Area Improvement Association. Mailing of the notice to the referenced address will be deemed compliance with this provision, whether or not it is received by the Lake Highlands Area Improvement Association. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, in this district until there has been full compliance for that use with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city.

(b) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation. (Ord. 25852)

sections.title: Zoning Map
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-702.118. ZONING MAP.

PD 702 is located on Zoning Map Nos. D-9 and E-9. (Ord. 25852)
